articleTitle: Power system harmonics. Part 1. Harmonic sources
abstract: Harmonics have been present in power systems since the very early stages of AC system development. The first part in this series of tutorials deals with harmonics from nonlinear power converters. Future parts will cover measurements, calculation, harmonic problems and harmonic reduction.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application of a 138 kV 200 MW braking resistor
abstract: The background to the application of a 138 kV 600 MW braking resistor, actually three banks at 200 MW each, on the BC Hydro system in order to meet design stability requirements is described. The design and construction of the resistors is then discussed briefly. The original resistor banks were installed in the 1960s, but one was replaced in 1987 with a new type of resistor. A load test was run on site to verify the capability of the resistor, and the test and its results are described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Material progress in cable accessories up to 33 kV
abstract: Accessories for both paper-insulated and polymeric-insulated power cables up to 33 kV have seen major changes, with modern materials such as cold pour resins, cold shrink systems, moulded rubber components and new tapes with specialised electrical properties being introduced. These new materials, in conjunction with the latest mechanical connecting systems, have gradually replaced traditional techniques like sweating, plumbing, taping, use of hot poured bitumen etc., with resulting reduction of installation times. This article explains the design philosophies behind some of the latest accessories, looking at the important electrical and mechanical properties of modern materials and the reasoning behind their choice.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The many faces of demand-side management
abstract: The article gives an overview of the technical and economic factors which have led to an increasing take-up of demand-side management in the energy market and the associated development and implementation of appropriate technologies.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: HV overhead line-the Scandinavian experience
abstract: Experience in both laboratory and practical situations in Finland, Sweden and Norway appears to confirm the advantages of 11/12 kV and 22/24 kV BLX covered overhead lines compared with conventional bare conductor (BLX is taken from the Norwegian 'Belagt Linesystem', or overhead line system, insulated with XLPE.) The line consists of a stranded, alloyed aluminium conductor with cross-section from 50 mm/sup 2/ to 150 mm/sup 2/, covered with a cross-linked and UV resistant polymer. The conductor is grease filled during the manufacturing process to make the covered cable watertight and corrosion proof. The development has taken off very quickly in Norway and Sweden since ABB Norsk Kabel launched BLX in 1989. The author discusses the construction of the lines, lightning protection, and the benefits of the BLX overhead lines.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Pulse converters in traction applications
abstract: After over a century of electric traction, the virtual monopoly of the commutator motor is drawing to a close. Major advances in devices and techniques have made the application of polyphase induction motors to traction units a viable proposition. The authors describe how the use of pulse power converters in these units can improve the electrical performance even further.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Test operation of phosphoric acid fuel cell plant
abstract: After overcoming major start-up problems, guarantee test runs were successfully completed in February 1993 on the phosphoric acid fuel cell plant (79 kW/sub dc/ 4 kW/sub th/) installed at the SWB solar hydrogen facility in Neunburg vorm Wald, Germany. The fuel cell plant comprises a fuel cell, a steam reformer with CO shift converter, and a pressure-swing adsorption unit. This article describes the fuel cell plant in detail. The most significant results of the guarantee test runs and specific knowledge derived from operation up to August 1994 are reported. The fuel cell plant described in this article was set up for testing within a solar hydrogen demonstration facility. In designing the plant, efforts were undertaken to incorporate an extensive variety of operating capabilities.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Implementation of a medium-scale CHP scheme
abstract: A typical medium-scale CHP project of about 50 MWe capacity, located on an industrial site which has a large heat and electricity load, is considered from a commercial and contractual standpoint. The essential elements of the scheme are identified and the role of the various parties who will need to become involved in the implementation and future operation of the scheme are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new medium/low voltage transformer for use in rural public distribution networks
abstract: This article describes the development of a new pole transformer, designed to be unexplodable in the case of an internal fault, to be better adapted to withstand changing loads and to be compact. Laboratory bench tests led to the choice of the best suited liquid dielectric, silicone, combined with temperature-insensitive aramid fibre. An unusual constructive step was the designing of a tank made of injection-moulded aluminium with a built-in high-current fuse. A series of tests were undertaken by the Laboratoires des Renardieres on a number of transformers with simulated faults of different kinds. The results of these tests were used to check the validity of the original design options.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Complying with the Code of Practice on legionella
abstract: The two most frequent sources of legionella are neglected air conditioning cooling towers and domestic hot water sources. All engineers who are involved with these (and other) water systems therefore need to know what the present legal position is and how risks from legionella can be minimised. Here, the authors describes how engineers can comply with the Code of Practice on legionella.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Where do we stand on cable standards?
abstract: The world of standards can often seem at best confusing to the average engineer, and at worst it is a jungle that is totally impenetrable. This article cuts into the confusion concerning cable standards and describes the present legislative position and the roles of BSI, IEC and CENELEC.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electrification projects in developing countries
abstract: In developing countries, attitudes and work patterns are very different from those in the industrialised world. Differing cultural and educational practices are factors which make the undertaking of electrification projects far from effective. The author argues that if projects are to succeed in the future there must be much closer co-operation and understanding between the developing nations and their industrialised partners.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The Holyhead experience (demand side management)
abstract: The Holyhead Powersave project was the first DSM exercise of significant size in the UK. Initiated by Manweb plc, long before the regulatory reviews of the electricity market, the project has proved beneficial to customers, the environment and utility alike. This town has become the subject of intense interest from utilities, regulators and governments throughout the world. The project is described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Digital communications for protection. III. Fibre optics
abstract: For pt.II see ibid., p.97 (April 1994). This tutorial describes the basic principles of fibre optics together with an outline of some of the practical considerations necessary in setting up a fibre optical system for transmission of digital data. The tutorial is the third in a series of three which describe the role of digital communications and fibre optics in power system protection.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Digital communications for protection. II. Teleprotection systems
abstract: For pt.I see ibid., p.281, Dec. 1993. This tutorial describes power system relay protection systems employing telecommunications. In this part the authors begin by considering the types of teleprotection systems and the different communication media that can be employed including pilot wires, private data circuits, power line carrier systems, microwave radio links, fibre optic links and wideband. They look at some of the international communication protocols and standard interfacing equipment (between digital signals and communication media) that are available.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Use of PME earth terminals on overhead distributors
abstract: The designer of an electrical installation will take into account the nature of the electrical supply to which his design is to be connected, so that the resultant system is safe. This article draws attention to the potential dangers of employing earth terminals provided to consumers with overhead LV supplies, and suggests that, for shock protection, an RCD may represent a safer alternative.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electrical trade-offs for GTO thyristors
abstract: With the much improved design and processing technology realised in recent years, GTO manufacturers have been able to offer improved device performance particularly relating to reduced snubber requirements. This has enabled system engineers to reduce the overall losses but at the expense of increased power dissipation within the device. This aspect, combined with the trend toward air-cooled systems which are much less efficient than an equivalent freon or oil-based heat exchanger, has pushed the device manufacturers to further reduce their device losses so that the junction temperature is maintained below the current maximum limit of 125 degrees C. This article discusses the important trade-offs in GTO electrical parameters with device design features, and details the associated merits and demerits of each. Particular emphasis is placed on the device losses.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Upgrading the Anglo-Scottish interconnection
abstract: This article is a summary of a number of papers presented at an IEE Colloquium in Glasgow on the upgrading of the power system interconnection between Scotland and England. The work involved ScottishPower, Scottish HydroElectric and National Grid Company in a multi-discipline project which, from authorisation to commissioning took 34 months, with a total investment of Pounds 125 million from the Scottish companies. The capacity of the interconnector has been increased from 850 MW to 1600 MW and this has been achieved by the integration of several complementary developments, including the construction of the longest transmission line to be built in the UK in 25 years (125 km), three new substations, two static VAr compensators (SVCs) and modifications to the excitation and automatic voltage regulators (AVRs) at three Scottish power stations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Regulating the electricity industry for energy efficiency
abstract: Demand-style management measures have the potential to reduce the costs of maintaining and operating the distribution system to the benefit of all customers. This article reviews how The Office of Electricity Regulation (OFFER) is seeking to promote energy efficiency in the UK on several fronts, including DSM.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The drivers behind the UK experience of DSM
abstract: The competitive forces driving demand-side management technology in the UK are based on the premise that customers demand energy services from their electricity supplier. This demand has considerable potential to be exploited for DSM measures. This article compares the drivers for DSM in the UK and the US and considers some of the potential communications solutions from UK manufacturers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electric railway traction. Part 3. Traction power supplies
abstract: Power is transmitted to electric railway locomotives and vehicles using DC or single-phase AC networks. The parallel development of traction technology in industrialised countries has led to a plethora of different electrification systems. This article covers the electrical engineering aspects of DC and single-phase AC traction power transmission systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: DC, induction, reluctance and PM motors for electric vehicles
abstract: Electric vehicle production is expected to increase dramatically over the next 10 years. DC motors are used exclusively at present but the change to AC brings advantages in weight and efficiency providing improved range. Because it is readily available, the induction motor is being used for the next generation of electric vehicles but the brushless DC motor has the lightest weight and highest efficiency and is expected to be used within the next 10 years. The switched reluctance motor also has merits for special applications. The author compares the different types of motor for weight, efficiency, cost and other factors. The author also discusses generators for hybrid electric vehicles.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electric railway traction. I. Electric traction and DC traction motor drives
abstract: This series of tutorial articles explains the electrical and control engineering background in electric railways. The articles cover traction drives with DC and AC traction motors, electrification systems, and railway signalling and control systems. This first article covers the nature of the traction load, the requirements of the traction duty cycle and power electronic controlled traction drives using DC machines.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electric railway traction. II. Traction drives with three-phase induction motors
abstract: For pt.I see ibid., Feb. 1994. This article describes DC-fed and AC-fed railway traction drives with three-phase induction motors, including the operation of the CSI, VSI and pulse converter. The dynamic performance of VSI-fed drives depends on the accompanying motor control scheme; two different arrangements are described: vector control with pulse-width modulation (PWM), and direct self-control.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Reactive power-real or imaginary?
abstract: No matter how abstract the concept of reactive power is, requiring as it does the use of 'imaginary' algebra to calculate, it plays a vital role in the stable operation of power systems. The author explains what reactive (or imaginary) power is and its effects on components and generator design. The author then discusses the early generator developments of Charles Parsons, high voltage transmission, reactive power control in transmission systems, and measurement of reactive power.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Power electronics in HVDC power transmission
abstract: This article describes the function and the hardware of a typical scheme for high-voltage direct current power transmission. Its basis is a 2*500 MW back-to-back scheme to interconnect the Western and Southern power regions of India. This technology permits sophisticated and rapid control of power system quantities-power, reactive power, frequency and voltage-by adjusting the timing of thyristor valve firing in relation to AC system voltage. The latest high-voltage thyristor and convertor control equipment is described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The rationale for demand-side management
abstract: Demand-side management has been practised for many years by North American utilities, encouraged by consumer pressure groups and regulators. With increasing demands to optimise the return on generation and network assets in the UK electricity industry and pressures to reduce environmental pollution, the potential of DSM to deliver such benefits while retaining the profitability of electricity companies is now under consideration.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Overhead transmission lines-refurbishment and developments
abstract: This article summarises the position with regard to National Grid Company's transmission system and the changes to it to meet the rapidly changing demands of electricity generation and transmission in England and Wales. It then outlines NGC's principal objectives for developments relating to overhead lines and comments on how these relate to the latest thinking within countries active in CIGRE.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The impact of EMC regulations on mains-connected power converters
abstract: The EC directive has brought many more classes of equipment within the realms of EMC regulations. This article discusses the circuit techniques that can be used to reduce harmonic currents conducted into the mains and examines some of the difficulties that switch-mode power electronics presents in terms of high-frequency electromagnetic emissions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Variable-speed drives-the future
abstract: Most variable-speed-drive (VSD) development is directed towards AC drives and it is likely that, for the foreseeable future, the rectifier-inverter and induction motor combination will dominate the market. This article looks at current technologies and future trends in VSDs including packaging, power semiconductor devices, silicon management, control methods, self tuning systems, communication protocols, power quality/EMC, and matrix and resonant converters.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: High-voltage earthing system design and performance
abstract: The earthing system of an electricity substation is of the utmost importance, primarily to ensure electrical safety for persons working within or near the substation and also to limit any electrical interference with third-party equipment to acceptable values. Adequate forethought can help prevent unwanted surprises and avoid unnecessary and sometimes retrospective expenditure to achieve an adequate earth grid impedance value. The process starts with accurate soil resistivity measurement and the derivation of an electrical equivalent of the soil structure at the site. This in turn enables the options for achieving an adequately designed grid to be assessed in order to find the most economic solution.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Power electronics R&D funded in the UK by SERC and DTI
abstract: The most prominent UK government support for power electronics research originates from the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) and the Science and Engineering Research Council (SERC). The importance of the power electronics sector in the UK was recognised in 1989 by the establishment of a dedicated LINK programme. This LINK programme is jointly funded by SERC and DTI and is entitled Power Electronic Devices and Derived Systems (PEDDS). A number of important projects have been supported under this programme, some of which are already completed, and further proposals are being considered. The author discusses the motor drives, power supplies, devices and process control applications which have been finded by the LINK PEDDS programme.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
